name: Peter Thiel

summary.text: Peter Thiel is a venture capitalist who co-founded PayPal and Palantir Technologies, which he chairs, and is a partner at Founders Fund. He made the first outside investment in Facebook and sat on its board from 2005 to 2022. FEC records show he gave $15 million in 2021 and 2022 to Protect Ohio Values, a super PAC supporting JD Vance's 2022 Senate campaign.

facts.claim: Thiel was born in Frankfurt in 1967. His father, Klaus, was a chemical engineer whose work took the family abroad, and Thiel attended seven elementary schools in California, Namibia, Ohio and South Africa. The family settled in Foster City, California; Fortune puts the move to the Bay Area in 1977, when he was 10.

facts.claim: In the 1970s Thiel went to a German-language school in Swakopmund, South West Africa (now Namibia), while his father worked at a nearby uranium mine, which The Namibian names as Rössing. Max Chafkin's 2021 biography, as summarised by The New Republic, says the family also lived in Johannesburg.

Edmondson of the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, then joined Sullivan & Cromwell in New York and left within a year to trade derivatives at CS Financial Products, a Credit Suisse unit. He told Bloomberg Markets he lasted at the law firm seven months and three days, and traded derivatives and currency options for a little more than a year.

facts.claim: Thiel has been managing member of Thiel Capital Management, LLC since September 1996. Bloomberg Markets reports that he started it as a macro fund with $1 million raised from friends and family, struggled to attract investors without a track record, and had more than $4 million under management by early 1998. No public record found of its investors' names or its trades during the 1997 Asian crisis or the 1998 Russian default and LTCM collapse.

facts.claim: In December 1998 Thiel Capital International, LLC, managed by Thiel's Thiel Capital Management, made Confinity a $100,000 bridge loan at 4.3% interest. In 1999 the loan was converted into 500,000 shares of Confinity Series A preferred stock. Bloomberg Markets reports that Thiel invested $240,000 in the company in total.

facts.claim: Thiel Capital International received 2,424,785 PayPal Series AA preferred shares in the March 2000 Confinity merger, transferred all of them in private transactions in 2000, then bought 1,455,133 Series AA shares in 2001. As of September 30, 2001 Thiel's pecuniary interest in the fund was about 45%. The filing does not name the counterparties.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (PayPal filing)
sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: PayPal (then X.com) sold 36,363,367 Series C preferred shares at $2.75, raising $100.0 million in March and April 2000. Its prospectus says the financing closed the day after the March 30, 2000 X.com-Confinity merger. The Nasdaq Composite had set its record close of 5,048.62 on March 10, 2000, so the round closed about three weeks after the peak, not before it.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (PayPal filing)
sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering
Nasdaq Composite Closes at 5,048.62

facts.claim: Colleagues credit Thiel with pushing the $100 million round through because he expected the dot-com bubble to burst. Bloomberg Markets reports that he raised more than planned at a $500 million valuation and closed on March 31, 2000. Sacks told Fortune that Thiel pushed to get the round closed and that the market crashed a couple of days later.

sources.title: Macro Man, by Deepak Gopinath (copy hosted by celestri.org)
Peter Thiel disagrees with you

facts.claim: Max Chafkin's biography reports that one of the first things Thiel did after returning as PayPal CEO in 2000 was to propose that PayPal turn over all its cash to Thiel Capital, his hedge fund. According to Chafkin, the board rejected the idea, objecting to risking the company's limited cash on speculation that could personally enrich the CEO. Fortune reported that Thiel refused to respond to the book's fact-checking questions; no public response from Thiel to this account was found.

sources.title: The Making of Peter Thiel's Networks: A Review of Max Chafkin's 'The Contrarian'
'The Contrarian' book review: Peter Thiel is a protean powerbroker

facts.claim: In August and September 2001 PayPal issued 4,500,000 non-voting Class A shares at $0.30 a share ($1.35 million) in which Thiel received a beneficial interest. PayPal lent him $1,350,000 on full recourse at 8% interest, of which he used $843,750 for 2,812,500 of the shares and pledged those shares as collateral.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (PayPal filing)
sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: PayPal's IPO of February 14, 2002 sold 5,400,000 new shares at $13.00, all from the company; the underwriters excluded sales by existing investors. Thiel beneficially owned 2,776,949 shares (5.1%) before the offering and 4.6% after, and officers and directors signed 180-day lock-ups. No public record found of Thiel selling shares in the IPO.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (PayPal filing)
sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Prospectus (Form 424B4), initial public offering

facts.claim: eBay's August 2002 merger filing lists Thiel as beneficial owner of 2,268,580 PayPal shares (3.7%). It says he agreed to vote for the merger and to limits on transferring his shares, and that the IPO lock-up expired on August 14, 2002. Fortune puts his take from the $1.5 billion sale at about $55 million; Bloomberg Markets says $60 million.

facts.claim: Thiel spoke at the July 2016 Republican National Convention, where he was described as the first openly gay speaker at a Republican convention in nearly a generation. In October 2016 a person close to Thiel said he would give $1.25 million, split between super PAC contributions and direct gifts to the Trump campaign; CNBC and the Boston Globe described it as his first gift in support of Trump's election.

facts.claim: In the 2022 midterms Thiel gave $15 million apiece, across multiple donations, to Protect Ohio Values, the super PAC backing JD Vance, and to Saving Arizona, the super PAC backing Blake Masters; CNBC put his total 2022 midterm spending at about $32 million. 12News reported that FEC records showed Thiel's $15 million was 92 percent of Saving Arizona's funding. Vance won; Masters lost to Mark Kelly.

facts.claim: In April 2023 Bloomberg and other outlets reported, citing people close to Thiel, that he did not plan to donate to any political candidates in 2024, with former employees named as an exception. The reports attributed the decision to his objection to the Republican Party's focus on social issues, and said the plan was not final.
facts.quote: Thiel had told associates he is not planning to donate to any political candidates in 2024, according to two people close to the businessman

Bloomberg Government reported a separate February 2026 filing showing a $1.5 million donation to Club for Growth Action.

facts.claim: Asked at the Cambridge Union in May 2024 about Israeli military use of AI targeting, Thiel said his bias was to defer to Israel, that the IDF gets to decide what it wants to do, and that they were broadly in the right.

Neither report says Thiel attended those meetings. The Jerusalem Post, citing Bloomberg sources, described Thiel as close to Netanyahu.

facts.claim: In June 2017 Thiel spoke to an invited audience of Israeli entrepreneurs at the Peres Center for Peace and Innovation in Tel Aviv-Jaffa. Haaretz's headline summarised his message as too much copying and not enough innovation in Israeli high-tech.

facts.claim: In September and October 2025 Thiel gave a four-part, off-the-record lecture series on the Antichrist at San Francisco's Commonwealth Club, organized by the nonprofit Acts 17 Collective, with Peter Robinson of the Hoover Institution moderating. Fortune reported the lectures would not be transcribed or shared with the public and drew on René Girard, under whom Thiel studied at Stanford.

facts.claim: The New York Times reported in June 2025 that in 2015 and 2016 Epstein put $40 million into two funds managed by Valar Ventures, a New York firm co-founded by Peter Thiel, and that the investment was worth nearly $170 million according to a confidential financial analysis of Epstein's estate reviewed by the Times and a statement from a Valar spokesperson. The Times described the Valar stake as the largest asset still held by the estate.

facts.claim: A 2023 Wall Street Journal review of Epstein's emails and schedules, as reported by the Daily Caller, found that Epstein scheduled at least six meetings with Thiel at his New York townhouse from 2014 to 2016 after Reid Hoffman's effort to connect the two. Thiel told the Journal: 'I was rather naive, and I didn't think enough about what Epstein's agenda might have been.' A Thiel spokesperson told The New York Times that Thiel 'never went to Epstein's Island.'

facts.claim: Daily calendars released by House Oversight Committee Democrats on September 26, 2025, from Epstein's estate, list a lunch scheduled with Thiel on November 27, 2017. Al Jazeera noted that the calendars do not indicate whether the scheduled meetings with Musk, Thiel and Bannon in fact took place, and that none of the three has been accused of wrongdoing related to Epstein.

A spokesman for Thiel denied to Byline Times that Epstein was a co-owner of the fund with Thiel, but confirmed that Epstein was a limited partner.

openQuestions: Irving Kristol as a funder of The Stanford Review in 1987: Wikipedia cites George Packer's The Unwinding (2013, p. 125), and New Left Review and other opinion pieces repeat it (some name the Olin Foundation). Not verified from a source opened this session. The New Republic, summarising Chafkin, names only Intercollegiate Studies Institute grants.

Speechwriting for former Education Secretary William Bennett (c. 1993-96) appears in Wikipedia and Independent Institute biographies, but every primary page that would confirm it (independent.org, Simon & Schuster, InfluenceWatch) was blocked by bot checks this session. Unverified.

Names of Thiel Capital Management's 1996 friends-and-family investors, its returns, and any positions during the 1997 Asian crisis, the 1998 Russian default and LTCM, or the 2000-2002 dot-com crash: no public record found. Bloomberg's 2004 piece 'Big Bucks From Bubble Fears' may say more but was paywalled (HTTP 403).
Counterparties to Thiel Capital International's 2000 private transfers of its PayPal Series AA shares and its 2001 purchase of 1,455,133 shares are not named in the prospectus.

Whether Thiel or Thiel Capital International sold PayPal shares between the August 14, 2002 lock-up expiry and the October 2002 eBay closing. The eBay S-4/A says 'one or more' of the listed holders had sold, without naming them. A Form 4 or 144 search on EDGAR could settle it.

Secondary accounts (ChainCatcher and PANews, retelling Chafkin or the podcast 'No Rivals') say the 2000 proposal was to move PayPal's new $100 million to Thiel Capital International to short the market, and that Michael Moritz threatened to resign. Not confirmed from a primary or major-outlet source.
New Zealand's Department of Internal Affairs released Thiel's citizenship file (1 February 2017 release, PDF), which may document his residence history. The archived copy could not be retrieved.

No Haaretz or Times of Israel report of a direct Thiel-Netanyahu meeting in 2024-25 was found. Calcalist and Ynet (September 2025) say some executives in Thiel's Jerusalem wedding party met Netanyahu without naming Thiel; the Jerusalem Post calls Thiel 'close to Netanyahu' citing Bloomberg sources. A Prime Minister's Office readout naming attendees would settle it.
The Bilderberg Steering Committee page was read from a cached copy; confirm Thiel's current listing on bilderbergmeetings.org. The year he joined the committee is not stated on the site.

The FEC receipts for Saving Arizona PAC (Thiel's $15 million) were not opened this session; the figure rests on CNBC and 12News citing FEC records. Axios reported a further $2.5 million in October 2022 while NBC reported no post-primary Thiel money; the FEC filings would settle the timing.
Michael Kratsios's title at Thiel Capital differs between sources (ExecutiveGov: principal, CFO and chief compliance officer; Homeland Security Today: chief of staff).
The quoted line from the 2016 RNC speech comes from press coverage rather than a transcript opened this session.
The original New York Times article (June 4, 2025) is cited through its Boston.com and Virgin Islands Daily News syndications; confirm against nytimes.com.
Reconcile Byline Times' $15 million Southern Trust Company commitment (by June 2015) with the Times' $40 million total; the fund names and the estate's exact valuation date were not found.
The June 2014 dinner date (June 9 or 10) and Thiel's reply quoted by some outlets ('very Israeli and very stimulating') could not be tied to a citable primary document; check the DOJ release.
The Wall Street Journal's 2023 story is cited through the Daily Caller's account; verify the quotes against the Journal.
